https://hungarytoday.hu/4ig-ceo-holds-ta.text: 4iG CEO Holds Talks on U.S. Partnerships in Space Gellért Jászai, Chairman and CEO of 4iG Plc., held a series of meetings in Washington with U.S. government officials and strategic industry partners to strengthen the company’s transatlantic partnerships in space, defense, energy, and digital infrastructure, he announced in a LinkedIn post on Thursday. Gellért Jászai said the meetings focused on concrete next steps and strategic cooperation opportunities “at a time when geopolitical and macroeconomic developments make strong transatlantic partnerships more important than ever.” During the visit, the 4iG CEO met with representatives of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), including Conor Coleman, Head of Investments, and Christopher P. Vincze, a member of the DFC Board. The discussions covered 4iG Group’s regional activities, digital infrastructure strategy, and potential investment opportunities. Together with the leadership of 4iG Space and Defence Technologies, Gellért Jászai also met with Michael J. Vaccaro, Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs. The talks focused on the ITAR regulatory framework and the company’s efforts to maintain high standards of transparency, compliance, and trust as a long-term partner of the U.S. defense industry. At Lockheed Martin, he discussed the progress of ongoing programs with Howard B. Bromberg, Vice President. At Northrop Grumman, he met with President Stephen O’Bryan to review the status of the HUSAT geostationary satellite program and the next steps in defense industry cooperation. The 4iG CEO also held talks with Kam Ghaffarian, founder of Axiom Space and X-energy, regarding developments in X-energy’s small modular reactor (SMR) technology. 4iG is an investor in Axiom Space and X-energy. Gellért Jászai said the Budapest-based company remains committed to building long-term partnerships with U.S. allies that create value for Hungary, the region, and the broader transatlantic community. Related article 4iG Completes $100 million Investment in Axiom Space Axiom Space, headquartered in Houston, is one of the leading global players in commercial human spaceflight and space infrastructure development. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm04.text: Image source, Reuters/DOJ Image caption, A recording device (R) was wrapped in toilet paper and plugged into a TV (L) By Laura Cress Technology reporter Published 5 hours ago A Saudi national who worked for OpenAI appeared in court this week for allegedly planting a secret recording device behind a TV in one of the tech giant's meeting rooms. Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer, was arrested by the FBI and charged with using or attempting to use a device "to intercept oral communications". As yet, it is not clear what he was planning to do with the recordings. But, here's we do know so far. Help from a chatbot The engineer asked AI to help him listen in to discussions about AI, according to an official complaint (the document filed in court). Between 17 August and 16 September, Alfozan had reportedly asked a productivity AI assistant several questions about meeting rooms and their availability. Some detailed in the complaint include "how about external partners, where would they usually meet with OpenAI at" and "can you list today's meeting in this room". The complaint also claimed that in September, Alfozan used a chatbot associated with his spouse to ask how to build and install a recording device and how to access it remotely. Alfozan had worked at the firm for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant a recorder. The room where the device was found was regularly used to hold meetings to discuss "highly confidential technical, commercial and strategic information" as well as OpenAI's "government engagements and commercial relationships", the complaint stated. Alfozan had no authority to access or be involved with meetings in the room, the complaint states. But CCTV footage recorded him near the conference room on eight separate occasions in September. Hiding in plain toilet paper On 30 September, OpenAI staff discovered a "surreptitious audio recording device" behind a television - which had been wrapped in toilet paper. A camera was placed in the conference room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering the room and appeared to look behind the television where the device had been inserted. The complaint also stated that same day he allegedly left an unattended bag in a different room. When security personnel opened it, it was found to contain "another recording device" similar to the one discovered, as well as Alfozan's wallet and ID. In a post on X , external , OpenAI wrote it had used its own AI models to "understand the device and where it had come from". It also said: "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data." Image source, Reuters/DOJ Image caption, Alfozan was captured looking behind a television where a device had been inserted Who is Abdulrahman Alfozan? Alfozan had been employed as an engineer by OpenAI since July 2025. The complaint said he was educated in the US and has been a legal permanent resident since 2020. He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI has been terminated. Alfozan's lawyer William Pernik told the BBC: "Like countless Americans, Mr Alfozan came to this country years ago as a young person with a dream. "These allegations appear wholly out of character for him, and we will relentlessly investigate all evidence produced by the government in this case to understand what actually happened, who was responsible and any possible reasons why." Pernik added: "In the meantime, we respectfully ask everyone to withhold judgment until full facts become known. Like every one of us, Mr Alfozan is presumed innocent, and what has been made public is an accusation, not a finding of guilt." On Tuesday, Alfozan made his initial appearance in a federal court in California. A detention hearing is scheduled on 19 October to determine whether he should remain in custody while proceedings continue. The FBI investigation is ongoing. If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (Â£190,000) fine. Sign up for our Tech Decoded newsletter to follow the world's top tech stories and trends. PEFA: Business Outlook arrives in Brasov: leaders of the business environment and public institutions, gathered for competitiveness, investments and regional development (P) Business & Investments Economics News Latest News Published on October 1, 2026 By Magda Purice Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email The European Business Women’s Employers’ Association PEFA and SME Brașov organize, with the support of the Brașov City Hall, a new edition of the national project Business Outlook – Together for the future , dedicated to the dialogue between the business environment, authorities and economic leaders. The event will take place on October 5, 2026, starting at 10:00, at Cinema Modern Brașov, and will bring to the fore three essential themes for the regional and national economy: competitiveness, investments and regional development. Andreea Negru, president of the European Business Women’s Employers’ Association – PEFA, emphasizes the role of cooperation between the private sector and public institutions: “The competitiveness of an economy is not built individually, but through trust, investments and the ability to bring the business environment, the administration and local communities to the same table. Through the national Business Outlook 2026 project, we want to build exactly this space for dialogue. Brasov is one of Romania’s important economic poles, with strong industry, entrepreneurship, human capital and real investment potential. I believe in an economic leadership that not only identifies problems, but brings people together to build solutions.” In her turn, Lorena Stoian, First Vice-President of PEFA , highlights the need for a predictable economic environment that supports the development of companies: “Entrepreneurs need predictability, access to finance, infrastructure and public policies connected to the economic reality. Regional development means capitalizing on the advantages of each community and creating the conditions for local investments and companies to generate long-term value. Business Outlook is about connecting ideas, resources and people who can transform economic potential into concrete development.” Business Outlook Brașov brings together representatives of the central and local public administration, leaders of employers’ organizations, companies, the financial-banking sector and professionals from strategic fields, in an applied dialogue about the current economic challenges and about the solutions needed to accelerate development. For Alina Paul, president of SME Brașov, regional development must be built starting from the real needs of entrepreneurs and from the competitive advantages of Brasov: “Brasov has all the premises to strengthen its position as a regional economic pole. In order for this potential to turn into sustainable economic growth, a constant collaboration between the private sector and the public administration is needed. Through Business Outlook, we bring together the relevant voices of the economy to discuss concretely what we can do better and about projects that can generate development, jobs and competitiveness.” Business Outlook – a national platform for economic dialogue Under the concept “Together for the future”, Business Outloo k is a platform through which PEFA brings the economic debate closer to entrepreneurial communities and regional development centers. After the editions organized in Sibiu and Craiova, the project arrives in Brasov, and will continue in Iasi. https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/scie.text: A Slovak student has developed an affordable microscope system that can create 3D models of tiny objects without destroying samples. Filip Lajciak, from Secondary Technical High School Dubnica nad Vahom, developed the system as a stereo vision solution for microscopic samples. It uses a stereo camera integrated into an optical microscopic effector to capture views from multiple angles.The images are processed to generate disparity maps, which are then used to create point clouds and 3D models. The system is designed as an affordable alternative to expensive laser scanning microscopes. According to Fairfolio, the project was presented at ISEF 2026 in the Embedded Systems category, where it received a First Award of $6,000 and the Dudley R. Herschbach SIYSS Award.How does the microscope create 3D models without destroying tiny objectsThe system was developed to address limitations in 3D scanning. 3D scanning of microscopic objects relies on laser scanning microscopes, which can be inefficient or unusable when samples need to be viewed from multiple angles. The project uses stereo vision by placing a stereo camera into an optical microscopic effector. The camera collects views as it rotates around the sample.These views are used to generate disparity maps, which provide data for 3D reconstruction. The system is designed to create non-destructive 3D reconstructions from multiple viewing angles. The project lists welding lines and irregularly shaped objects among samples that can be difficult to analyse using laser scanning microscopes. The approach focuses on making this scanning more affordable and accessible.How did the scannerâs design change through its developmentThe student developed several versions of the hardware during development. The initial version used a rigid aluminium frame measuring 350 Ã 500 Ã 600 mm. It included 3D-printed rotary guide rails and 3D-printed NEMA-17 cycloidal actuators. A stereo camera was integrated into individual microscope lenses, allowing the lenses to rotate around the microscopic sample during scanning.Later versions were approximately half the size and introduced custom motorised optical effectors to make the system more modular. This allowed the scanner to be integrated with an industrial robotic arm. The hardware evolved through several iterations, with each version refining the design while retaining the stereo scanning approach. The subsequent setup was smaller, more modular, and compatible with an industrial robotic arm.The technology used to turn microscopic images into 3D modelsThe system turns captured microscopic images into 3D information through processing steps. Stereoscopic images are processed using semi-global matching to generate a disparity map. The disparity map is then converted into a point cloud through triangulation. Image processing and additional transforms are computed on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano SBC.Through a parallel GPIO connection, it interfaces with a Teensy 4.1, which controls the actuators. The software was developed using the Robot Operating System, or ROS. It publishes data channels to RViz, a graphical user interface used to monitor camera images, disparity maps, point clouds, and the system state. The acquired data are processed into a 3D model.Potential uses of the microscopeâs 3D modelsThe resulting 3D model can be used for detailed cross-sectional visualisation and analysis of internal structures without destructive sampling. The project identifies applications for the scanner. These include the analysis of micro-particle structures, biological samples and material defects.The system is also intended for samples such as welding lines and irregularly shaped objects, where multi-angle views can be difficult to obtain with conventional approaches. The project was entered in the Embedded Systems category at ISEF 2026. It received a First Award of $6,000 as well as the Dudley R. Herschbach SIYSS Award and Herschbach SIYSS Award.The work combines a stereo camera, optical microscope components, motorised hardware, and software processing in one system to produce 3D models of microscopic samples.
